rules.roads: Natural Earth 1:10m roads in the map's countries, sampled every 1.6 km and snapped to links between hex centres. Class 0 (motorway): every road Natural Earth flags as an expressway. Class 1 (major road): the other roads of the European E-road network, and the other highways (Natural Earth types Major and Secondary Highway, Beltway, Bypass) at scale rank 7 or less, where no motorway already joins the same two hexes. Route names: the national number (A6, M7) where Natural Earth has one, else the E-road number (a bare national number shows as "Route 8"); where several routes share a link the lowest number wins. Lines stop at the borders of neighbouring countries; ferries are left out.
rules.rail: Natural Earth 1:10m railways at scale rank 7 or less, snapped to links between hex centres; main lines are scale rank 5 or less. Lines stop at the borders of neighbouring countries. Natural Earth carries neither operator nor traffic, and its alignments are older and sparser than today's network.
rules.ports: Every port reporting to Eurostat that handled at least 500,000 tonnes of goods (gross weight, unloaded plus loaded) in its country's latest complete year, ranked by tonnage. Each port is placed at the Wikidata place carrying its UN/LOCODE, else at the UN/LOCODE list's coordinates, else at the GeoNames town of its name. Ports Eurostat reports as one authority are drawn at their main harbour (Antwerp-Bruges at Antwerp, HAROPA at Le Havre). Rows that are not one place ("other ports", offshore installations, Estonia's confidential total) are left out, and so are ports on islands too small for a hex of their own.
rules.airports: Every airport reporting to Eurostat with at least 50,000 passengers in the year (arrivals plus departures, scheduled and charter), placed by its ICAO code with OurAirports. Hub classes follow passengers: large 10 million or more, medium 2 to 10 million, small 500,000 to 2 million, regional under 500,000. Airports on islands too small for a hex of their own are left out; Tirana (Albania) has no figures at Eurostat and is missing.
